//: OpenBox observe-only hooks (STORY-SL-4; unified engine STORY-SL4-WIRE-2). Each hook shells out to the bundled Go engine as `bin/openbox hook claude-code <event>`, which maps the payload to a normalized OpenBox event and spools it locally (no network on the hot path). The hook always exits 0 with empty stdout, so it can NEVER block a tool call or inject context (INV-3 / D7). SessionEnd additionally flushes the spool to OpenBox. The event name is passed as the argv subcommand (deterministic, independent of the payload).
//preToolUseRewake: PreToolUse registers a SECOND handler, `openbox rewake claude-code`, with asyncRewake (E9-S5). It runs in the background — it cannot block, so it cannot be the gate — and exits 2 only when an approval this call filed is decided AFTER the gate already denied, at which point its stderr reaches the model as a system reminder. In the ordinary case it finds no filed approval within a 5s grace and exits 0. Its 2700s timeout covers core's 30-minute approval window; nothing waits on it. See adapters/common/hookflow/rewake.go for the marker protocol the two handlers coordinate through.
//preToolUseTimeout: PreToolUse carries a 30s ceiling (E9-S4) because it is the only gating hook, and so the only one that can hold for an approval decision. The ceiling is not a delay: the engine spends it only when a high-risk class (shell/MCP) escalated and core filed an approval — see hookflow.AwaitApproval. Every other hook keeps the tight 5s. Claude Code's matcher cannot express 'raise this for these tools only' without negative-lookahead matching its docs do not promise, so the ceiling is raised per HOOK and the class narrowing lives in the engine. Keep this in lock-step with claudecode.preToolUseHookTimeoutSec, which the enforce budgets derive from (installer_test pins the two together).
